einzeiler: Matt Levine and Mary Childs discuss mortgage refinancing, law firm billing, and ETF…
kurzfassung: Matt Levine and guest Mary Childs explore how AI tools could reshape mortgage refinancing and professional service business models. They also analyze an FTC complaint against Amazon's advertising auctions and a tax-avoidance strategy using S&P 500 ETFs. The conversation highlights how automated systems and shifting incentives disrupt traditional financial and corporate structures.
stichpunkte: AI tools could make mortgage refinancing much faster and more common, potentially driving up base mortgage rates and increasing borrowing costs.
The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage relies heavily on borrowers exercising their prepayment options suboptimally.
Law firms and investment banks face pressure to abandon traditional hourly billing and associate-heavy apprenticeship models as AI automates routine tasks.
The FTC filed a complaint against Amazon, claiming its sponsored product auctions deceive advertisers by using a hidden soft reserve price.
Art auctions use a similar practice known as chandelier bidding, where auctioneers place phantom bids to meet undisclosed reserve prices.
Foreign hedge funds exploit timing differences between the dividend payout dates of nearly identical S&P 500 ETFs to dodge dividend withholding taxes.

kapitel.titel: AI Impact on Law Firms and Apprenticeship Models
Amazon Ad Auctions and Chandelier Bidding
ETF Dividend Swaps and Tax Strategies

Matt and guest host Mary Childs discuss CDS gossip, suboptimal mortgage refinancing, cheap options, shopping for savings accounts, billing by the hour, AI and the apprenticeship model, second-price auctions, chandelier bidding, the IVV to VOO pipeline, rich person trades vs. hedge fund trades and how much we all miss Katie.
